clips.send: A friend who panics the moment something goes wrong, because an old parable about a runaway horse proves the 'disaster' is often the rescue in disguise - calm, hope.
clips.caption:
A poor farmer's son forgets to lock the corral. The family's only horse runs off. 'This is terrible,' the son says. 'Bad? Maybe. Maybe not,' the father answers.

The horse comes back the next day with ten wild horses behind it. The son tries to break one, gets thrown, breaks his leg. 'Terrible,' the neighbors say. 'Bad? Maybe. Maybe not.'

The next day the army comes through the village taking every able-bodied young man to a war most of them won't survive. They can't take the son. His leg is broken.

clips.send: A friend who thinks they have to choose between being successful and being spiritual, because he wore the businessman mask for decades to hide exactly who he really was - curiosity, relief.
clips.caption:
People started noticing his eyes had changed color - dark brown for decades, suddenly blue, hazel, green. He finally gave the real answer: he'd taken off the veil.

For most of his life he put on a costume on purpose - the businessman, the marketing genius, the guru - because people only follow a teacher who looks like he's already won. Underneath it the whole time was a different identity he'd never revealed.

You don't have to pick one. Wealth and spiritual depth were never opposites - that was always the lie.
